elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Harpoon shall ..." — both triggers, for any reason, with no request or anticipation condition.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Insertion provides assistance "for a period of at least ninety (90) days"; no six-month duration is stated. Repair: change the period to up to six (6) months.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause is silent on pricing; no "at Harpoon's then-current rates" language appears. Repair: add the rate basis to limb (a).

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to AbbVie all data and Information belonging to, supplied by, or generated for AbbVie".

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: No format specification in limb (b). Repair: add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion-and-certification limb; Section 9.7 only offers destruction-or-delivery at a Party's election as soon as reasonably practicable, and permits retained copies. Repair: add a limb (c) requiring deletion after return and written certification.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason" covers both natural expiry and termination, and both limbs run from that trigger.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "reasonable transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days following the effective date of such expiration or termination" — obligation on Harpoon (Vendor) in AbbVie's (Customer's) favour.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires Harpoon to "export and deliver" AbbVie's data and Information within thirty (30) days after expiration or termination; the 30-day clock runs from the termination/expiry event, not from a request.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback level: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (90-day assistance and 30-day export, both triggered by expiry or termination for any reason).

Preferred level is incomplete: the six-month assistance period, then-current-rates basis, machine-readable format and certified deletion after return are all absent — consistent with the drafter's stated fallback target, but the finding cannot be recorded as preferred.

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion for a clause that was genuinely missing; no existing language is deleted or paraphrased, and no extras (survival tail, at-own-expense, procedures, damages categories) are added. The 'reasonable' qualifier and the possession scope are necessary boundaries, not extras.

Intent is preserved: Section 9.7's request-based Confidential Information mechanic, the Section 12.7 reversion and the Section 12.10.2 sell-off rights are untouched, and the new export duty does not contradict 9.7's permitted retained copies (the insertion imposes no deletion obligation).

Drafting point to verify (not a failure as scored): limb (b) uses capitalised "Control", which in this agreement is an IP-licensing concept rather than data possession. Confirm the defined term resolves as intended, or replace with lower-case "control" to avoid an off-point or dangling defined term.
Optional upgrade if the counterparty engages: adding "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to limb (b) costs little and moves one preferred element without disturbing the fallback structure.
